annotations.text:
These tokens now ship in the real code — this sheet and the app are in sync.

Source of truth:
app/src/theme/{colors,typography,spacing}.js
web/tailwind.config.js

Both carry identical values, so a brand change is an edit to those two files and nothing else. There are zero hardcoded hex values in userapp/src and zero stock Tailwind palette classes in vendor-website/src.

One judgement call worth knowing: text-secondary #52666A carries body copy, and muted #829497 is reserved for timestamps and placeholders — muted is ~3:1 on white, below AA for anything you actually have to read.

Sample data, not real records.

Shop names, ratings, review counts, distances, prep times, order IDs and OTPs are placeholders chosen to make the layouts legible.

Worth knowing: ratings, reviews, distance, shop photos, prep time, saved addresses and payment-method selection have NO backend behind them today. The API returns none of these, so these screens are ahead of what's built.

The vendor actions here follow the real order lifecycle: Accept → Start Printing → Mark Ready → Verify OTP → Complete.

One difference: 'Start Printing' is a step the backend doesn't have. Today an order goes accepted → ready_for_pickup with no separate printing status, so the customer's tracking screen infers 'Printing' from 'accepted'.

Both codebases are now READY for it: a 'printing' status is defined in userapp/src/theme/colors.js and web StatusBadge, with a comment saying nothing emits it yet. When the backend adds the enum value the badge renders correctly with no UI change — no fake API call was added to fill the gap.
